parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that \(f'(x) = \left(1 - \dfrac{x}{2}\right)e^{-x/2}\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that \(f''(x) = \left(\dfrac{x}{4} - 1\right)e^{-x/2}\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the stationary point of the graph of \(f\), and show that it is a maximum.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the point of inflection of the graph of \(f\). Justify your answer.

parts.label: e
parts.text: The tangent to the graph of \(f\) at the point of inflection meets the \(x\)-axis at Q. Find the coordinates of Q.

parts.label: f
parts.text: Show that the tangent to the graph of \(f\) at the point where \(x = a\) passes through the point \((c, 0)\) if and only if \(a^2 - ac + 2c = 0\). Hence find the set of values of \(c\) for which at least one tangent to the graph of \(f\) passes through \((c, 0)\).

idea: Use the product rule, with the chain rule for \(e^{-x/2}\). Since \(e^{-x/2} > 0\) for every \(x\), the sign of \(f'\) or \(f''\) is the sign of the bracket in front.

solution.label: d
steps: \(f''\) changes sign at \(x = 4\) (negative for \(x < 4\), positive for \(x > 4\)), so the concavity changes: this is a point of inflection.

solution.label: f
steps: It passes through \((c, 0)\) exactly when \(-ae^{-a/2} = \left(1 - \dfrac{a}{2}\right)e^{-a/2}(c - a)\). Divide by \(e^{-a/2} > 0\): \(-a = c - a - \dfrac{ac}{2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\), so \(a^2 - ac + 2c = 0\).
Some tangent passes through \((c, 0)\) exactly when this quadratic in \(a\) has a real root: discriminant \(c^2 - 8c \ge 0\), that is \(c(c - 8) \ge 0\).
So \(c \le 0\) or \(c \ge 8\). (With \(c = 8\) the only root is \(a = 4\): the tangent at the point of inflection, as in part (e).)

stem: The curve \(C\) has equation \(y = \dfrac{1}{x}\), for \(x \ne 0\). The point \(P\left(p, \dfrac{1}{p}\right)\), where \(p > 0\), lies on \(C\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the equation of the tangent to \(C\) at \(P\) is \(y = -\dfrac{x}{p^2} + \dfrac{2}{p}\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The tangent meets the \(x\)-axis at A and the \(y\)-axis at B. Find the coordinates of A and B in terms of \(p\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Show that the area of triangle OAB, where O is the origin, does not depend on \(p\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Show that P is the midpoint of [AB].

parts.label: e
parts.text: Let \(p = 2\). The normal to \(C\) at \(P\) meets \(C\) again at Q. Find the coordinates of Q.

parts.label: f
parts.text: Find the exact length of [PQ].

idea: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^{-1}\right) = -x^{-2}\), so the gradient at \(P\) is \(-\dfrac{1}{p^2}\). The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so its gradient is \(p^2\). To find where a line meets the curve again, substitute and solve; one root is the point you already know.

solution.label: e
steps: At \(P\left(2, \frac{1}{2}\right)\) the tangent has gradient \(-\frac{1}{4}\), so the normal has gradient 4: \(y = 4x - \dfrac{15}{2}\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the time taken if the lifeguard swims all the way, in a straight line from L to S, and the time taken if she runs 60 m first.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the total time is \(T(x) = \dfrac{x}{5} + \dfrac{\sqrt{(60 - x)^2 + 900}}{2}\) seconds.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find \(T'(x)\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the value of \(x\) that minimises the time, and the least time.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Justify that your answer to part (d) gives a minimum.

parts.label: f
parts.text: Now let the swimming speed be \(v\) m s\(^{-1}\), where \(0 < v < 5\). Show that the time is least when \(60 - x = \dfrac{30v}{\sqrt{25 - v^2}}\), provided this value of \(x\) is positive.

idea: Time is distance divided by speed for each stage. Set \(T'(x) = 0\); the square root can be removed by squaring once the equation has been rearranged with the root alone on one side.

solution.label: a
steps: Swim all the way: \(LS = \sqrt{60^2 + 30^2} = \sqrt{4500} = 67.08\ldots\) m, at 2 m s\(^{-1}\) that is \(33.54\ldots\) s.
Run 60 m (12 s), then swim 30 m (15 s): 27 s.

solution.label: b
steps: Running \(x\) m takes \(\dfrac{x}{5}\) s. P is \(60 - x\) m along the shore from the point opposite S, so \(PS = \sqrt{(60 - x)^2 + 30^2}\), which takes \(\dfrac{PS}{2}\) s.

solution.label: d
steps: \(T(46.90\ldots) = 25.74\ldots\) s (a GDC graph of \(T\) gives the same minimum).

solution.label: e
steps: \(T'\) changes from negative to positive, so this is a minimum. It is also less than both end values from part (a), so it is the least time on \(0 \le x \le 60\).

solution.label: f
steps: \(d > 0\), so \(d = \dfrac{30v}{\sqrt{25 - v^2}}\). (Check with \(v = 2\): \(\dfrac{60}{\sqrt{21}} = 13.09\ldots\), as in part (d).)

stem: The region \(R\) is enclosed by the curve \(y = \dfrac{2}{x}\) and the line \(y = 3 - x\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the points where the curve and the line meet.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest vertical distance between the line and the curve within \(R\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Show that the area of \(R\) is \(\dfrac{3}{2} - 2\ln 2\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: The region \(R\) is rotated through \(360°\) about the \(x\)-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid formed.

idea: Between the meeting points, the line is above the curve, so the vertical distance is \(3 - x - \frac{2}{x}\): maximise it, or integrate it for the area. When the region is rotated, each slice is a washer: an outer disc from the line minus an inner disc from the curve.

stem: A train travels in a straight line between two stations. It leaves the first station from rest and stops at the second station 60 seconds later. Its velocity is \(v(t) = \dfrac{t(60 - t)}{60}\) m s\(^{-1}\), for \(0 \le t \le 60\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the maximum velocity of the train.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the train when \(t = 10\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the distance between the stations.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the average speed of the train.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Find the length of time for which the train travels faster than 12 m s\(^{-1}\).

parts.label: f
parts.text: To shorten the journey, the velocity is changed to \(v(t) = kt(T - t)\), for \(0 \le t \le T\), where \(k\) and \(T\) are positive constants. The distance between the stations is unchanged, and the magnitude of the acceleration must never exceed 1.2 m s\(^{-2}\). Find the least possible value of \(T\).

idea: Acceleration is \(v'(t)\) and distance is \(\int v\,dt\) (the velocity is never negative here). In part (f), write both conditions in terms of \(k\) and \(T\), use the distance to remove \(k\), and find where the acceleration is largest.

solution.label: a
steps: \(v'(t) = \dfrac{60 - 2t}{60} = 0\) at \(t = 30\), and \(v(30) = \dfrac{30 \times 30}{60} = 15\). (The graph of \(v\) is an inverted parabola, so this is the maximum.)

solution.label: f
steps: Acceleration: \(a(t) = k(T - 2t)\), which goes from \(kT\) down to \(-kT\), so the largest magnitude is \(kT = \dfrac{3600}{T^2}\).

stem: Let \(f(x) = \dfrac{ax + b}{x^2 + 1}\), for \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants. The graph of \(f\) has a stationary point at \((2, 1)\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that \(f'(x) = \dfrac{a - 2bx - ax^2}{\left(x^2 + 1\right)^2}\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of \(a\) and the value of \(b\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the other stationary point of the graph of \(f\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Hence write down the range of \(f\), given that \(f(x) \to 0\) as \(x \to \pm\infty\).

parts.label: e
parts.text: Find the set of values of \(k\) for which the equation \(f(x) = k\) has exactly two solutions.

idea: Use the quotient rule. The two facts about \((2, 1)\), that it is on the graph and that the gradient there is 0, give two equations for \(a\) and \(b\). The number of solutions of \(f(x) = k\) is the number of times the horizontal line \(y = k\) crosses the graph.

solution.label: d
steps: \(f\) is continuous, has only these two stationary points, and tends to 0 at both ends. So its greatest value is 1 (at \(x = 2\)) and its least value is \(-4\) (at \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\)).

solution.label: e
steps: \(f(x) = 0\) only at \(x = \frac{3}{4}\). For \(x < \frac{3}{4}\), \(f\) is negative: it falls from near 0 to \(-4\) at \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\), then rises to 0. For \(x > \frac{3}{4}\), \(f\) is positive: it rises to 1 at \(x = 2\), then falls back towards 0.
So a line \(y = k\) with \(-4 < k < 0\) or \(0 < k < 1\) crosses the graph twice; \(k = -4\), \(k = 0\) and \(k = 1\) give one solution each; other values give none.

stem: Water flows into a tank at a rate of \(r(t) = 30t\,e^{-0.2t}\) litres per minute, where \(t\) is the time in minutes after the inflow starts. At \(t = 0\) the tank holds 200 litres, and from \(t = 0\) water also leaks out at a constant 20 litres per minute.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the time at which the rate of inflow is greatest, and find this greatest rate.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the volume of water that flows in during the first 10 minutes.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the two times at which the volume of water in the tank is neither increasing nor decreasing, and describe how the volume changes between \(t = 0\) and the first of these times.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the greatest volume of water in the tank.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Find the time at which the tank becomes empty.

idea: The volume changes at the rate \(r(t) - 20\), so \(V(t) = 200 + \displaystyle\int_0^t \left(r(u) - 20\right)du\). The volume is greatest where \(r(t) = 20\) and \(r\) is falling through 20.

solution.label: a
steps: \(r'(t) = 30e^{-0.2t} - 6te^{-0.2t} = 6e^{-0.2t}(5 - t)\), which is zero at \(t = 5\) (positive before, negative after).

solution.label: c
steps: The volume is steady when \(r(t) = 20\). With a GDC: \(t = 0.7790\ldots\) and \(t = 15.84\ldots\)
Before \(t = 0.779\ldots\) the inflow is less than the leak, so the volume decreases (slightly, to \(192.6\ldots\) litres).
solution.answer: \(t = 0.779\) and \(t = 15.8\) minutes; the volume decreases at first

solution.label: d
steps: The volume increases while \(r(t) > 20\), for \(0.779\ldots < t < 15.84\ldots\), and decreases afterwards, so the greatest volume is at \(t = 15.84\ldots\)

solution.label: e
steps: After \(t = 15.84\ldots\) the volume falls, because the inflow keeps decreasing towards 0.
